PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Restore peer chats lost after session refresh
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #339409.

### What changed

- Revert #339074 in full, including its Codex continuation UI, model/account plumbing, telemetry, and supporting storage APIs. This intentionally removes the entire feature, not just the URI-resolution change.
- Restore fragment-free backend session resolution. Selecting a peer chat must not register its chat fragment as a separate backend session.
- Automatically recover erased peer-chat membership for verified affected local Copilot CLI sessions, retaining original chat URIs, surviving transcripts, and provider continuation metadata.
- Remove verified phantom registrations without deleting their shared backing storage, and refresh recovered list projections before the first session-list response, including after a restart.

### Why

The fragment-bearing resolution introduced by #339074 can register a phantom session separately from its real parent, while both use the same path-based local database. The phantom writes an empty peer-chat mirror; subsequent legacy reconciliation can erase the parent's authoritative membership. Reverting prevents the corruption, but does not repair membership already lost.

### Recovery safety and limitations

- Recovery requires a restore-created phantom, a matching registered parent, and surviving selected-chat backing metadata. Additional candidates require affirmative parent membership evidence; healthy catalogues are not scavenged.
- Respect explicit deletions, authoritative ownership elsewhere, and concurrent membership changes. Do not rewrite child transcripts or chat-local provider metadata, and do not create missing child databases.
- Persist the pre-recovery membership and a completion marker. Interrupted recovery uses frozen candidates; completed recovery does not resurrect later removals.
- Preserve existing order and archive state. Missing peers are appended deterministically and restored as active because their original order/archive flags cannot be reconstructed.
- Legacy directory names are only recovery evidence, not authoritative current ownership; this does not require redesigning stable chat identities or chat moves.

### Validation

- `npm run compile` - passed.
- `npm run hygiene` - passed (12,895 files checked).
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostPeerChatStore.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostDatabase.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSessionRegistry.test.ts` - passed: 792 passing, 16 pending.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - passed.
- Previously validated recovery against 91 isolated SQLite backup copies: 23 affected peers recovered; healthy catalogues, 86 child databases, and 110 foreign membership rows unchanged. No manual changes to live storage.
- Verified recovery in the installed build, including preserved author/reviewer transcripts. Regression tests cover first-list visibility for live, cold, and already-completed recovery; the new cold projection tests failed on the pre-fix implementation.

CI build [480291](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480291) hit an intermittent macOS managed-settings diagnostics timeout also reproduced on main in builds [480293](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480293) and [480122](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480122). That failure is being investigated separately.

Build [480297](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480297) is still running on the temporary integration-test recovery-bypass commit. The bypass has been reverted; that build is not validation of the current head. Recovery remains enabled in tests. A full cross-platform CI run on the current head has not yet completed.

To test manually, start the fixed build against an isolated copy of affected storage with a verified restore-created fragment registration and an empty peer-chat mirror. The initial list should show recovered peers without opening the parent; opening a recovered peer should load its original transcript. Refresh/restart should retain membership without duplicating it, and subsequent intentional removals should stay removed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path, default-enabled catalog path, one-call-per-candidate cardinality, cold-process cache behavior, and database-wide serialization are explicit in code. Exact milliseconds vary by catalog size and disk cache, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: serialized SQLite queries and decoded chat-row objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On the first list in each agent-host process, cost grows as one `getSessionChatCatalog` query per eligible local Copilot CLI session, plus all peer rows returned; the database's single `Sequencer` makes the effective query concurrency 1 despite the limiter of 4.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased first-session-list and startup latency for users with large local Copilot CLI catalogs
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The list path fetched all eligible `sessions_v2` rows with the single bulk `readMany`/`listSessionsV2` query and did not read each session's chat catalog separately.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After the bulk read, the added loop awaits `_refreshRecoveredSessionProjection` for every eligible local Copilot CLI session not yet checked; that helper immediately calls `getSessionChatCatalog(sessionKey)`, even for healthy sessions that never underwent recovery.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `centralResults[index] = await this._refreshRecoveredSessionProjection(...)` line places a per-session catalog lookup, through `_refreshRecoveredSessionProjection`, directly after and on the critical path of the existing bulk catalog read.
Findings.Title: Batch the recovery projection check before listing sessions
Findings.Impact: Opening the Sessions UI or requesting the initial session list after each restart now blocks on N additional serialized SQLite queries for N local Copilot CLI sessions. Large catalogs therefore lose the bulk-read startup behavior this path otherwise preserves; the in-memory checked set only helps later lists in the same process.
Findings.Evidence: `AgentHostCatalogListReader.readMany` issues one `listSessionsV2(sessions)` query. The added call at 3768 reaches `_refreshRecoveredSessionProjection`, whose first operation is `this._orchestratorDatabase.getSessionChatCatalog(sessionKey)`. `AgentHostDatabase.getSessionChatCatalog` queues one SELECT through the database-wide `_transactionSequencer`, so all candidate calls serialize and each materializes that session's chat rows. Candidate selection includes every eligible, non-external local `copilotcli` parent, not only sessions with a recovery marker.
Findings.Recommendation: Perform one batched chat-catalog lookup for all candidates and compare in memory, or persist/query recovery candidates in bulk so healthy sessions are excluded before any per-session read; keep the existing per-session synchronization only for mismatches that are known to have completed recovery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial Sessions list after agent-host startup with a healthy local Copilot CLI catalog
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registry enumeration and the bulk `sessions_v2` read complete first; the added recovery-projection candidate loop is then fully awaited before list results can be returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SQLite query for all registered candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This single bulk query was the central-catalog listing cost.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before list metadata is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read authoritative peer-chat catalog and all chat rows for one session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query for every eligible non-external local Copilot CLI parent on the first list in each process, even when it was never recovered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-session chat-catalog read followed the bulk listing query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All calls are awaited before the list can proceed and serialize through the database-wide sequencer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of eligible local Copilot CLI parent sessions, plus the peer rows materialized by each query.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The loop uses a limiter of 4, but `getSessionChatCatalog` queues through one `AgentHostDatabase._transactionSequencer`, so effective SQLite concurrency is 1.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `_checkedRecoveredSessionProjections` avoids repeat work only for later lists in the same process; it is empty after every restart. Healthy matches are positively cached; read/parse failures are not.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: candidate cardinality, awaited critical path, query implementation, default-enabled catalog mode, and serialization are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact delay depends on catalog size, SQLite page cache, and storage speed; large long-lived catalogs are the realistic worst case.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out; submitted one medium-severity finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: First list repairing fragment-registration peer-chat corruption
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When a restore-created fragment registration exists, recovery runs before normal catalog listing and must finish or fail per parent before the list advances.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the entire session-data directory and enumerate all child directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per affected parent; `_recoverChatSelectionCorruption` processes parents serially, so P parents cause P full directory enumerations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The list path did not scan session-data directories for peer-chat recovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the first list while recovery candidates are discovered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the parent database, read recovery/legacy/title metadata, open candidate backing databases, and read provider metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parent open per affected parent and one backing open per suffix-matching candidate that passes ownership evidence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No repair-time per-candidate database inspection occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before recovery can verify phantoms and listing can continue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/update central chat membership, write the legacy mirror/completion marker, and unregister verified phantoms.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one recovery transaction and mirror update per affected parent, plus one unregister per verified phantom.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Corrupted membership remained unrepaired and phantom registrations remained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to make repaired membership visible in the first response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of affected parents P, total session-data directories N, and surviving peer candidates C; directory discovery is O(P*N), with candidate database work bounded by matching parent suffixes and catalog limits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parents are processed serially; candidate database opens inside a parent are also sequential. Central database mutations are sequenced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful recovery writes a completion marker and unregisters verified phantoms, so subsequent lists normally skip the path. Malformed evidence preserves the phantom and retries on later lists; there is no negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the I/O and scaling mechanism; lower for user-visible magnitude because this is an exceptional repair path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Affected users and parent counts are limited to the corruption cohort; a typical repair is expected to be one-shot. Malformed persistent evidence can repeat the scan, but prevalence and directory counts are uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the broad scan is tied to one-time recovery evidence and no high-confidence material delay beyond the reported normal-list fan-out was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restart after recovery completed but the central list projection is stale
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same cold projection check first compares central membership. A mismatch then opens the parent database to read the completion marker and synchronizes the projection before returning the list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the durable completion marker from the per-session database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only for sessions whose authoritative membership differs from the projected peer list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No recovery completion marker was consulted during listing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines whether a stale projection may be refreshed before response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read authoritative peers, build/write a synchronized catalog payload, and re-read the refreshed row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per mismatching session with a completed recovery marker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A stale central projection could be returned without this synchronization work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fully awaited so recovered peers appear in the first response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of previously recovered sessions whose projected peer list remains stale.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Candidate wrappers allow 4, while central orchestrator DB operations serialize; per-session databases may overlap.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A successful refresh enters the process-local checked set. Missing/incomplete markers are cached as checked; read errors are retried on future lists.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The mismatching completed-recovery cohort should be small and the synchronization is required for first-list visibility.
Scenarios.Verdict: The necessary mismatch refresh is not separately reported; the finding targets the avoidable per-session checks imposed on every healthy candidate before mismatches are known.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening/restoring a Codex session after model metadata and continuation plumbing are reverted
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Explicit restore activates Codex, requests authoritative thread metadata, materializes provider backing, and restores history. The changed model fallback is downstream of this existing restore boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start and initialize the Codex app-server when explicit restore crosses the activation boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced persistent connection per activated provider process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restore already activated and retained the app-server.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request `thread/read` metadata/history from the Codex app-server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata read and, depending on history mode, paginated or full history reads for the opened session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: `_getSessionMetadataForRestore` already requested authoritative metadata with `activation: 'restore'` before materialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh Copilot model catalog when no model catalog is populated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Coalesced by `_modelsRefreshPromise`; not per restored session while warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can be joined by restored-model resolution, but the diff did not establish a new call on the normal restore path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Opened sessions and model-catalog coldness; provider connection and refresh promises coalesce work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold session reads are limited; connection startup and model refresh are coalesced/sequenced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm model and discovered-thread caches avoid repeated enumeration; explicit restore still obtains authoritative metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the traced production call order.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Direct isolated materialization behavior changed, but the production restore path performs the existing activation/read first, so no independent added boundary was proven.

Scenarios.Scenario: Removal of Codex continuation notices, spotlight adapters, storage CAS APIs, and model-picker guided opening
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The feature contributions and UI/service hooks are removed; remaining picker and spotlight flows use their prior generic paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of workbench windows, visible notices, spotlight steps, and model-picker opens.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Removed coordinators/listeners no longer schedule work; no new limiter or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Deleted continuation storage coordination and account/session candidate caches no longer participate.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The diff mostly removes work and behavior, so any performance effect is neutral or beneficial.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 92 changed files and the performance-sensitive call paths. Submitted one finding for the newly introduced cold-list per-session SQLite fan-out. Recovery repair I/O, Codex restore boundaries, UI removals, IPC/storage removals, and cache/lifecycle behavior were traced without another high-confidence diff-caused performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
